rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. I have no answer for that.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. Keep it brief.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. Speak plainly.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. I have no advice to offer.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger? The weather is no concern at the gate.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You need not trust me, stranger. Keep your distance from the gate.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now. New, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, offering your hands before you’ve even crossed the approach? I’m set for the moment, but what brings you this way?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Well now, asking a gate guard to weigh in on his captain. Roderic keeps a fair watch, far as I’m concerned—what’s your interest in him?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, advice from a man on patrol? Keep your hopes modest; that's all I've got for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, you’ve found a fine patch of weather to stand in. That all you’ve brought me?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Well now, you needn't. I'm only asking the question, not asking you to trust me.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New here? That's what you say. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? No. Keep to the road and don't make trouble.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? What are you asking me for?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Into the city? Ask someone else. I’ve nothing for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather's no reason to stop on the road. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You don't know me. Keep your distance and answer plainly.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, love, you’ve found me in the middle of tending the yard. I’m Hessa, and I’ve no news to give you just now.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I'm managing the yard well enough just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, Captain Roderic? Stiff as a gate, but fair. I like him.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, I’ve no advice to give you on that. These buckets won’t haul themselves, and the kitchen needs water before evening.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh, love, it is—makes the yard a pleasure to tend, at least.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, love, you needn’t trust me. I’m only here tending my yard.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I don't know what you mean by “this place.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: If you know your way around a forge, pick up the tongs. If not, keep clear of my work.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: What about him? I’ve got work to finish.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: What. I’ve no advice for getting into the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: What. Weather won't finish this work.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. Now, if you're buying, speak.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh! You're new? I—well, this is the smithy, and I'm helping at the forge, but Aunt Mara says I shouldn't chatter when there's work to do.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh! A hand? I mean, maybe—there's always something to do, but I can't think what just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh! The captain? I don't know enough to make anything of them, but now I'm wondering what they're like—have you met them?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, you need into the city? I don’t know anything useful about that, but I’d like to hear what it’s like inside!

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh! It is, isn't it? Makes the forge feel almost pleasant, and I should be getting back to the scrap—Aunt Mara hates it wasted.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh! You don't have to, not yet—I haven't even told you anything, have I?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I’ve no answer for you.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Mind the timber. A steady hand would do more good than advice just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I’ve work to finish, and no measure of the captain comes to mind.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Keep to the road and ask at the gate. I’ve no measure of what they’ll allow.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Mm. Better than rain on the timber, I suppose.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You needn't. I've work in front of me, and no time to dress it up.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! New to town, are you? What would it be worth to you to know?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, a willing hand has value—but I’ve no task to set you just now. What would you reckon your help is worth?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Friend, a captain’s worth is measured by the bargains he keeps. What’s your measure of him?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Friend, advice is a commodity, and I’ve none to spare without knowing its value. What can you offer for it?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend! Fine weather makes for pleasant trade, does it not?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Friend, trust is a risk like any other. What would make it worth your while?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Stranger. On foot. You said you're new here.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Stranger. Hands free, by the sound of it. I have no task for you.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Stranger. I have no report to make about the captain.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Stranger. You need the city. I have no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear skies. I can see the south road plainly.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I report what I see, nothing more.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Hm. New, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Hm. No.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Hm. Captain's the captain.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Hm. Ask someone else.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hm. Weather's weather.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Hm. Don't, then.
